claims.text: An article links to what came before it and cannot link to what came after, because the later article did not exist when it was written.
claims.quote: An article links to what came before; it cannot link to what came after, because that did not exist.

claims.text: 551 of the 566 links between the 105 articles point to an earlier article.
claims.quote: 566 links between 105 articles. 551 point to an earlier article.

claims.text: 15 links point forward, in 14 articles, and every one was added by an edit after the later article existed.
claims.quote: 15 point to a later one, in 14 articles.

claims.text: 94 of the 105 articles are cited by at least one later article, 551 citations in all, and 11 of those are answered by a link back.
claims.quote: 94 of the 105 articles are cited by at least one later article

claims.text: In 104 pairs of consecutive articles the later one links the earlier 42 times and the earlier links the later 7 times.
claims.quote: In 42 the later one links the earlier; in 7 the earlier links the later.

value.unit: consecutive pairs where the later links the earlier

claims.text: The most cited articles link forward least: the fractal semantic graphs article is cited by 23 later articles and links to none of them.
claims.quote: is cited by 23 later articles and links to none of them

claims.text: Link density has risen: the August articles average fewer than one link each to another article, the September ones about one and a half, and most October days between four and ten.
claims.quote: The five August articles average fewer than one link each to another article

claims.text: Every article already ends with a derived Threads section, Builds on and Continued by, so the forward path exists at the foot of the page.
claims.quote: Every article ends with a Threads section, derived from the links at build time

claims.text: The Continued by list is easy to miss for three reasons: it is at the very end, it carries no reason, and it has one kind for a sequel, a citation and a correction alike.
claims.quote: There are three reasons it is easy to miss.

claims.text: A forward link to a sequel is a convenience; a forward link to a correction is the record.
claims.quote: A forward link to a sequel is a convenience. A forward link to a correction is the record.

claims.text: Of the 97 articles whose history sgit.ai keeps, 62 have more than one version.
claims.quote: Of the 97 articles whose history sgit.ai keeps, 62 have more than one version.

value.unit: articles with more than one version

claims.text: A scan for sentences linking an earlier article near a word like correct, wrong, revised or no longer found 45 sentences, most using the words in other senses.
claims.quote: That second scan found 45 sentences; reading them, most use the words in other senses.

claims.text: Corrections come in three kinds: revised in place, corrected by a later article, and a status that has changed since.
claims.quote: What is left falls into three kinds.

claims.text: One clear case of a correction by a later article: the code review company article corrects the code review graph article on refactoring, and the earlier one points at it only in a list at the end.
claims.quote: the follow-up that answers a reader's seven questions and corrects this article on refactoring

claims.text: Status since, a plan in an older article that has or has not happened, is probably the most common kind of correction, and the kind of drift that turns into a quoted claim.
claims.quote: The quieter kind, and I think the most common.

claims.text: Every article should carry four kinds of forward link: What came next, Corrected by and Status since at the top, and Cited by at the foot.
claims.quote: What I would like, for every article, is to be able to see what came after it

claims.text: What came next is added by the release that publishes the later article, in the same commit.
claims.quote: Added by the release that publishes the later article, as part of the same commit.

claims.text: Cross-article links could carry a relation, continues, corrects or cites, so a validator could warn when a correction is not acknowledged by the earlier article.
claims.quote: so a validator could warn when a later article says it corrects an earlier one and the earlier one does not say so

claims.text: This release adds a What came next note to the top of the first three of the four articles written in a row on 13 October.
claims.quote: This release adds a What came next note to the top of the first three.

claims.text: Forward links should be added in turns from the most recent articles down, a few at a time, with the counts above as the baseline.
claims.quote: Start from the most recent articles and go down the line, a few at a time, taking turns with the new writing.

claims.text: The counts are of links written in the text; the generated Threads and Related lists are not counted.
claims.quote: The counts are of links written in the text.

claims.text: The correction scan is by words and would miss a correction that uses other words.
claims.quote: The correction scan is by words.

claims.text: The version counts are sgit.ai's; articles written in this repository since the move are not in the 97.
claims.quote: The version counts are sgit.ai's.

claims.text: The four kinds of forward link are a proposal; only the What came next notes on three articles are built.
claims.quote: The four kinds are a proposal.

claims.text: The counts come from a script over the source markdown of the 105 articles numbered in articles/ids.json at v0.12.23.
claims.quote: read by a script that parses article links
